item: S&P 500 +1.2% on the week, +14.2% YTD; record high early in the week. Energy and utilities led; tech flat.
10-year auction cleared at 5.30%, highest since 2000; long yields hit their highest in over two decades before easing.
September minutes: unanimous 0.25% hike; majority favours another move this year. Markets price a December hike.
Fed funds target raised to 3.75–4.00%, first hike in 3+ years, on oil-driven inflation and strong jobs.
Q3 S&P 500 earnings expected +29.6% y/y; 2026 +32.7%; 2027 +15.8%. 72 positive vs 44 negative guidance.
Analysts’ bottom-up 12-month index target 9,290 (+19.6%). 60% of stock ratings are Buy.
Oil +58.7% YTD: Mideast tension, Strait of Hormuz traffic down after attacks, hurricane shut-ins in the Gulf.
Doubts over returns on AI spending briefly hit tech; consumer sentiment at a five-month low.
Shiller CAPE at 41.9, second only to the December 1999 peak of 44.2.
US CPI and PPI (Sep), retail sales, industrial production, Fed Beige Book; big-bank earnings.
